proposal.title: Collection title
proposal.deciding_marker: The isolated nominal formula names the song and precedes the first-person desire beginning at 1:2.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not absorb the title into a chapter unit or use its relation to Solomon to decide authorship; the larger alternatives remain reviewable because the Hebrew relation formula is compact.
proposal.risk: Title syntax and relation are translation-sensitive; title separation is literary evidence only.

proposal.title: Opening desire, self-description, and shepherd question
proposal.deciding_marker: Kiss, fragrance, chambers, dark-but-lovely self-description, vineyard memory, and the question and reply about grazing form the opening address complex; 1:9 begins a sustained praise exchange.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not split automatically at WEB speaker labels inside 1:4 or at every addressee change; the opening dialogue is more coherent as one movement, while 1:2-2:7 remains the larger parent alternative.
proposal.risk: Speaker and number shifts are real evidence but supplied labels are not authority; preserve both the smaller opening poems and the larger exchange.

proposal.title: Reciprocal praise and delight through the first adjuration
proposal.literary_form: praise exchange and desire tableau closed by refrain
proposal.deciding_marker: The horse comparison opens reciprocal praise, fragrance, dwelling, flower, tree, banquet, embrace, and love-sickness imagery; the daughters-of-Jerusalem adjuration at 2:7 closes the movement across the chapter seam.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not let the chapter boundary or each speaker exchange divide the poem; retain the complete cross-chapter movement, with the two chapter-contained praise clusters as exact alternatives.
proposal.risk: Speaker turns and imagery transitions can support narrower poems, but the terminal adjuration makes the larger cross-chapter unit defensible.

proposal.title: Arrival and spring invitation
proposal.deciding_marker: The beloved's approaching voice opens the scene; repeated arise-and-come language, seasonal imagery, dove and vineyard appeals, mutual-belonging formula, and the closing gazelle call complete the movement.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not split at the quoted invitation's end or detach the foxes and mutual-belonging response; the arrival, invitation, and answering call function together.
proposal.risk: The speaker of 2:15 and force of 2:17 are disputed; the larger invitation remains preferable, with submovement alternatives preserved.

proposal.title: Night search, finding, and adjuration
proposal.deciding_marker: Repeated sought/did-not-find language, movement through the city, watchmen encounter, finding and holding, and arrival at the mother's house form one scene; the repeated adjuration closes it.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not detach the adjuration merely because it recurs elsewhere; here it closes the search scene, though a refrain-only row remains an exact alternative.
proposal.risk: The relation of the adjuration to the preceding dreamlike search is interpretively pressured; keep the complete scene and refrain together.

proposal.title: Wilderness procession and royal carriage
proposal.deciding_marker: The who-is-this arrival question opens a single visual catalogue of perfume, guard, carriage, materials, daughters, crown, and wedding-day summons, ending at 3:11.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not atomize the guard list, carriage construction, or daughters' summons; all serve the governing procession tableau.
proposal.risk: Identification and historical reconstruction of the procession are outside scope; the visual movement is clear even when referents are not.

proposal.title: First extended body-praise song
proposal.deciding_marker: Behold-you-are-beautiful opens an ordered body and beauty catalogue; 4:7 supplies a totalizing close before the come-with-me invitation at 4:8.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not split each body part or blank-line marker into separate chunks; the catalogue is governed by its opening and totalizing close.
proposal.risk: 4:6 may bridge the catalogue and garden/spice movement; retain the whole praise poem and preserve the larger 4:1-5:1 alternative.

proposal.title: Bride and garden invitation with response
proposal.literary_form: invitation, garden praise, opening call, and response
proposal.deciding_marker: Come-with-me and repeated bride address lead through love, fragrance, locked-garden, orchard, spice, and fountain imagery; 4:16 invites entry, and 5:1 answers with arrival and communal eat/drink closure across the chapter seam.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not detach the garden-opening invitation from the answering arrival because of the chapter boundary or a supplied speaker label; invitation and response are one complete lyric movement.
proposal.risk: The assignment and extent of voices at 4:16-5:1 are difficult; the cross-chapter invitation-response parent must remain intact and externally reviewable.

proposal.title: Second night search and daughters exchange
proposal.literary_form: failed encounter, search, adjuration, descriptive praise, and response
proposal.deciding_marker: Sleep/awake and knocking open a failed encounter; departure, watchmen violence, adjuration, daughters' question, beloved catalogue, renewed question, garden answer, and mutual-belonging formula form an extended dialogic search movement across the chapter seam.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not separate the body-praise catalogue from the daughters' question that elicits it, or the garden answer from the renewed search question; the exchange resolves at 6:3.
proposal.risk: The scene's coherence does not settle dream, plot, speaker identity, or violence interpretation; several exact submovements remain plausible.

proposal.title: Tirzah-Jerusalem praise and unique beloved
proposal.literary_form: renewed praise catalogue and climactic acclamation
proposal.deciding_marker: The Tirzah/Jerusalem comparison begins renewed praise; body images, queens and concubines, the unique dove, and the who-is-she solar-lunar acclamation reach a climax at 6:10 before the garden descent.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not detach the enumerated women or final acclamation from the governing praise movement; the catalogue develops from direct praise to public acclamation.
proposal.risk: The speaking group at 6:10 is uncertain, but the praise form and closure before 6:11 are strong.

proposal.title: Garden descent and return call
proposal.literary_form: garden recollection and contested return exchange
proposal.deciding_marker: First-person descent to inspect budding growth moves through the compressed chariot/desire line into the fourfold return call and answering question; 7:1 begins a new body-praise catalogue in WEB numbering.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not force 6:12 into a continuous plot or make WEB's chapter seam decisive; retain 6:11-13 as the ambiguous garden/return movement while preserving the MT/English numbering pressure at 6:13-7:1.
proposal.risk: This is a highest-difficulty seam because 6:12 is obscure, voices shift, 'Shulammite' appears, and versification places the following line differently.

proposal.title: Second extended body-praise song
proposal.deciding_marker: Feet-in-sandals begins an ascending catalogue through thighs, body, breasts, neck, eyes, nose, head, hair, stature, palm, fruit, breath, and mouth; 7:10 changes to a first-person mutual-belonging response.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not split every body image or supplied speaker turn; the catalogue remains one praise song, while the 6:13 incipit alternative is preserved because of versification and address.
proposal.risk: The poem's beginning may include the second half of 6:13 in other numbering/traditions; 7:9 also contains a voice-sensitive pivot.

proposal.title: Mutual belonging, countryside invitation, and final adjuration
proposal.literary_form: reciprocal affirmation and invitation closed by refrain
proposal.deciding_marker: The mutual-belonging formula opens a countryside and vineyard invitation, stored-fruits gift, wish for public intimacy, mother's-house leading, embrace, and the shortened daughters adjuration that closes the movement across the chapter seam.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not let the chapter boundary divide invitation from continued desire, and do not automatically detach the adjuration; the repeated refrain supplies the larger movement's close.
proposal.risk: The relation between countryside invitation, kinship wish, mother's house, embrace, and adjuration is debated; preserve both cross-chapter parent and exact submovements.

proposal.title: Wilderness emergence and love-seal poem
proposal.literary_form: arrival question and climactic love aphorism
proposal.deciding_marker: Who-is-this-from-the-wilderness opens an emergence tableau; apple-tree recollection leads directly to seal, death, fire, waters, and unpurchasable-love sayings, closing before the sister exchange.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not isolate the celebrated seal poem from the emergence and awakening frame without preserving the larger 8:5-7 parent; the frame and aphorism are literarily adjacent and mutually contextualizing.
proposal.risk: Voice assignment inside 8:5 and the relation of awakening/birth imagery to 8:6 are uncertain; the aphorism must not become detached proof text.

proposal.title: Little sister, wall or door, and answering self-claim
proposal.deciding_marker: The little-sister question opens a wall-or-door conditional exchange; the first-person 'I am a wall' answers the imagery and reaches peace/favor before the vineyard saying.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not detach the answer from the question or force identity/chronology among the voices; keep the compact exchange whole, with 8:8-12 as the larger alternative.
proposal.risk: Speaker identity, temporal relation, and social interpretation are unresolved and require external literary and Hebrew review.

proposal.title: Solomon's vineyard and the vineyard before me
proposal.deciding_marker: The Baal Hamon vineyard lease and thousand-silver account are answered by 'my own vineyard is before me' and its thousand/two-hundred reckoning; the garden address at 8:13 changes form.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not split the numerical account from its answer or decide whether vineyard is literal, bodily, economic, or symbolic; retain the saying as a formal contrast.
proposal.risk: Referents, possessives, economic logic, and relation to 1:6 are interpretively dense; the seam after 8:12 is plausible but not certain.

proposal.title: Final reciprocal calls
proposal.literary_form: closing call and answering departure invitation
proposal.deciding_marker: The garden-dweller is asked to let the voice be heard, and the answering come-away/gazelle call echoes earlier invitation imagery to close the book.
proposal.rejected_alternative: Do not split the two calls merely because supplied speakers differ; their reciprocal address and terminal echo make the pair the stronger closing unit.
proposal.risk: The two voices are grammatically and editorially assigned in different ways; the reciprocal closing function is stronger than a specific speaker reconstruction.

oversplit_premortem: Do not treat every grammatical gender or number change, vocative, supplied speaker label, poetic line, blank line, metaphor, or body part as a seam.
Do not detach an invitation from its response, a daughters' question from the praise answer it elicits, or an adjuration from the movement it closes without preserving the larger parent.
Do not let English chapter boundaries break 1:9-2:7, 4:8-5:1, 5:2-6:3, or 7:10-8:4.
Do not force a continuous drama, chronology, speaker cast, wedding reconstruction, allegorical scheme, or literalist scheme.
Do not fragment body-praise, spice/garden, procession, watchmen, or vineyard catalogues below their governing lyric function.
Do not use rare Hebrew, roots, qere/ketiv, WEB headings, or later reception as automatic boundary authority.

final_statement: This blind primary proposes 17 complete lyric movements covering Song.1.1-Song.8.14 exactly once. It prefers larger coherent poems and exchanges, preserves exact alternatives at disputed seams, and leaves speaker, translation, versification, interpretation, and theology questions non-authorizing and reviewable.
